records.region: Pitiquito, Sonora; La Inmaculada–San Ignacio drainage and Gulf of California coastal plain
records.material_pending_reason: The selected central alluvial continuation between the mapped upper San Ignacio reach and the southern Aribaipa receiving corridor remains unestablished. Upper connections, lower convergences and the Gulf terminal are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: San Ignacio is directly mapped on the upper and western receiving drainage, with La Inmaculada on the chosen eastern upper approach. The selected central southward alluvial passage to the Aribaipa corridor is not sufficiently established to apply San Ignacio as a completed representative name to the entire selection. No separate scalar name is assigned to that passage or the lower confluence branches.
records.completion_scope: Upper La Inmaculada–San Ignacio reach and lower Aribaipa/Cerro El Puerto-to-Gulf corridor correspond; the intervening selected plain transfer remains incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: San Ignacio is directly mapped on the upper and western receiving drainage, with La Inmaculada on the chosen eastern upper approach. The selected central southward alluvial passage to the Aribaipa corridor is not sufficiently established to apply San Ignacio as a completed representative name to the entire selection. No separate scalar name is assigned to that passage or the lower confluence branches.

scope_limits: San Ignacio is positively supported as a named mapped drainage, but the entire supplied selection cannot yet be represented by it with completed correspondence.
The meaningful remaining gap is the central alluvial branch transfer into the Aribaipa corridor. Neither a nearby name nor visible dry-fan membership substitutes for that connection.
Individual source and name-transition points, present discharge, exact banks, tidal mouth configuration and the operating role of modified features remain unassigned.
The terminal is geographically identified independently of the unresolved upstream transfer; no extension beyond the selected Gulf endpoint is added.

records.material_pending_reason: The selected opening, westward inland through-links, both fragment joins and the particular estuarine terminal passage remain unestablished by permitted independent geography.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection starts at its southeastern opening, first runs north, turns west across the inland reach, then turns north and continues to the Pacific coastal endpoint. Neither the nearby Iscuandé system nor a western Sanquianga outlet is substituted.
records.completion_scope: Primary authorial course and locality correspondence only; selected geographic through-links remain incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: Real whole-river candidate supported by primary authorial course description and coastal park prose. Complete selected-route correspondence remains unestablished; the name is not assigned uniformly to every opening, tributary or tidal passage.

scope_limits: Río Tapaje is a geographically plausible, source-supported candidate, not a completed representative-system identity.
The contractor copy is publicly readable but not authenticated against an institutional original.
Pulbuza, Taija, El Arrastradero and Martínez are bounded source observations, not aliases of Tapaje or newly selected features.
Remaining gaps concern ordinary-scale through-links, not exact banks, vertices, flow measurements or operating conditions.
Formal registry identity and Korean rendering remain unverified.

records.region: Central Cuba, Sancti Spíritus; Zaza basin and the southern coastal plain.
records.candidate_name_role: Regional receiving-river candidate supported by original university cartography and topology; not an accepted identity for the complete selected feature.
records.material_pending_reason: Missing selected opening/receiving join and continuous intermediate correspondence, partial Zaza-reservoir passage assignment, and unresolved lower westward coastal/wetland-to-sea connection. Available regional source context is insufficient to establish those links; the independent thesis and proposed detailed-map route became unavailable.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research pass completed with one source-material-pending result. The inspected independent regional maps and topology support named components but do not complete ordinary correspondence for the whole selected mainstem. This is not a completed representative-system finding or a completed name-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Zaza is supported for the named regional receiving system and its reservoir context. The complete selected opening, intermediate connections, reservoir through-link and final coastal approach remain unestablished. Jatibonico del Sur is separate eastern context, not an alternative name assigned to this object.

naming_scope_details.reservoir_context_limit: Only Zaza is relevant to the regional selected reservoir setting; no claim is made that the selection traverses the separate Tuinucú or Siguaney impoundments.
managed_connection_context: Small-hydropower component below the Zaza reservoir
excluded_inferences: No combined Zaza–Jatibonico scalar name is invented.
No tributary, reservoir, canal or neighboring basin is renamed after the representative candidate.
No current hydraulic operation, exact bank or shoreline, legal hydronym boundary, official source point or exact river-mouth vertex is required or claimed.
Discovery snippets from the unavailable thesis and catalogue are not substantive evidence.
The 122.513km value is preserved model metadata, not an official measured river length.

records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Readable imagery establishes the chosen headward valley, intervening river and lake passages, eastward turn, northeast lower corridor and actual coastal outlet at ordinary corridor scale. The inspected sources do not provide a supported natural-river hydronym. The coastal receiving-water names are not transferred to the river.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No supported representative natural-river name was established for the selected northern Victoria Island route.
records.completion_scope: The selected mainstem follows an unnamed northward valley and lake chain, turns east through a meandering lowland corridor, and continues northeast to the head of the western arm of Glenelg Bay. Glenelg Bay is a southwestern extension of Wynniatt Bay. Complete ordinary source correspondence supports a completed naming-scope hold with the river candidate left null.
records.supported_name_scope: No supported representative natural-river name was established for the selected northern Victoria Island route.

scope_limits: A completed naming-scope hold does not establish that this river or its lakes lack local or otherwise documented names.
The entire selected mainstem is considered as a representative river/lake corridor; distinct components are not forced to carry one scalar name.
The stage-three path generalizes meanders and the coastal display extension. Correspondence is at ordinary corridor scale, without exact bank, vertex, present-flow or hydraulic claims.
Snow, lake ice and patchy cloud limit small-detail interpretation but do not prevent the observed ordinary headward-to-coastal corridor correspondence.
No source capture-date or present-day legal-name assertion is made; Korean naming and formal registry status remain unset or unverified.

bounded_name_observations.role: Larger receiving bay of which Glenelg Bay is the southwestern extension

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
